punchline: The Stoics kept a reminder that they would die, not to feel gloomy, but to decide what was worth their time.
thirty_sec: There's an old Stoic phrase, memento mori: remember that you will die. It sounds bleak, but the idea, attributed to Mark Manson, is that it's practical. When time feels endless, trivial worries pile up and nothing has to be chosen. Facing the fact that it runs out does the opposite. It helps you drop what doesn't matter and pick what you actually value.
question: What would you stop doing this month if you took seriously that your time is limited?
